title: Dynamic fair slicer for continuous batching with KV-aware preemption
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a new 'dynamic fair slicer' component in the continuous batching runtime that enforces SLO-aware scheduling, proportional tenant fairness, and KV-cache-aware preemption at micro-batch granularity. The slicer should: (1) allocate token/SLA budgets per request, (2) slice requests into resumable micro-batches that fit current GPU memory and kernel shape constraints, (3) make preemption decisions that minimize KV cache invalidations, and (4) provide telemetry to quantify fairness and tail latency impact.
motivation: Current continuous batching preemption operates at coarse batch boundaries and ignores per-request KV cache cost. That causes large preemptions that evict hot KV entries and increases downstream cold-start token cost, hurting tail latency and unit cost for customers with tight SLOs. We need finer-grained, fairness-conscious preemption to keep latency SLOs while improving overall utilization.
technical_solution: Introduce a Slicer abstraction that accepts incoming requests and emits ordered micro-batches (slices) with metadata: token_count, predicted_kv_footprint, tenant_weight, deadline_budget.
Maintain per-GPU occupancy estimator that combines active KV bytes, model activation footprint, and projected micro-batch memory to determine safe pack size for each kernel shape.

Scheduling policy: proportional-share with deficit counters + earliest-deadline-first (EDF) for SLO-sensitive requests. Deficit counters ensure long-lived heavy tenants don't starve small low-latency requests.

Preemption policy: prefer yielding low-progress micro-slices from tenants with remaining deficit > 0 only when forced. On preemption, tag slice as 'paused' with resume pointer; avoid immediate KV eviction for paused slices for a configurable grace window to reduce cold KV misses.

KV-awareness: predict per-request KV usage using model profile + prefix-length heuristics. Use predicted_kv_footprint to prefer packing slices with complementary KV sets (hot + warm) to maximize re-use and reduce evictions.
Memory compaction: trigger light-weight compaction hooks when cumulative predicted memory crosses threshold; allow small prioritization of kernel shapes that reduce temporary activation allocations.
Instrumentation: emit slice-level metrics (slice_latency, slice_kv_hits, preempt_count, resume_count, tenant_deficit) to Console for per-tenant SLO dashboards and offline analysis.
Safety: fallback to existing continuous-batcher if model profile or KV prediction is missing; enable opt-in via runtime flag until stable.
acceptance_criteria: Slicer integrated in runtime and default disabled behind feature flag 'dynamic_slicer_v1'.
End-to-end unit and integration tests covering slicing, pause/resume, and KV-grace behavior.
Benchmark: 95th percentile token latency reduced by >=5% for mixed SLO workload in our internal replay compared to baseline, while throughput stays within +/-3%.
KV eviction rate decreased by >=10% in representative replay (measured as unique KV keys evicted per 10k tokens).
Telemetry available in Console: per-tenant slice_latency, preempt_count, kv_evictions, and deficit_balance.
Canary rollout plan documented and verified with canary traffic gating (metrics and rollback criteria).
implementation_steps: Design: finalize Slicer data model and API (1 week).
Prototype: implement Slicer + micro-batch resume semantics in a dev branch; smoke tests (2 weeks).
KV predictor: add lightweight heuristic predictor and caching layer; unit tests (1 week).
Scheduler: implement deficit-EDF policy in runtime with config knobs (2 weeks).
Memory estimator: integrate GPU occupancy estimator and packing heuristics (1 week).
Instrumentation: add slice-level metrics and dashboards (1 week).
Benchmarks & tuning: run internal replays, tune thresholds, iterate (2 weeks).
Canary rollout: staged rollout with rollback playbook (1 week).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: inaccurate KV footprint predictions could worsen eviction behavior. Mitigation: start with conservative overestimates and collect ground-truth KV usage to improve model.
Risk: added scheduler complexity may increase CPU overhead. Mitigation: micro-optimizations, C++ hot-path, and telemetry to measure scheduler latency; gate behind feature flag.
Risk: resumed micro-batches could blow tail memory if many accumulate. Mitigation: global cap on paused-slice memory; eviction of least-recently-paused slices beyond grace window.
Risk: fairness knobs misconfigured could starve heavy tenants. Mitigation: provide simulated tenant-share tests and a default safe configuration tuned on production traces.
qa_steps: Unit tests for slice creation, pause/resume, and resume pointers.
Integration test with KV service mock to assert grace window prevents immediate eviction.
End-to-end replay with mixed SLOs: measure 50/95/99 p99 token latency and compare to baseline.
Fault injection: force scheduler decision path to preempt repeatedly and observe graceful resume and stable KV metrics.
Load test: sustained 24-hour load with 3 tenant classes to observe fairness counters and memory stability.
notes_and_links: Related issues: ENG-17283 (KV accounting), ENG-18645 (GPU occupancy estimator)
